name: My Safety Plan
careNote: Handle with care. This app is a suicide-prevention safety plan, made by Daraja Studio in memory of Jerry's son Ryan. In this test you are NOT writing about yourself. You play a counselor showing how the plan works, and you type only the made-up example words given to you. If anything in this test brings up hard feelings for you, stop at any time — that is completely fine. Talk to your school counselor or a trusted adult. In Kenya you can also reach Befrienders Kenya on +254 722 178 177 (call, SMS or WhatsApp; daytime hours), and in an emergency call 999 or 112. Note: the blue button inside the app calls 988, which is the American helpline — it does not work from a Kenyan phone.
careNoteSource: Befrienders Kenya number checked 10 Oct 2026 on lifeline-international.com (Kenya page: helpline +254-722-178-177, call/SMS/WhatsApp, Mon–Fri 9am–5pm) and befrienders.org search listing (09:00–17:00). Hours differ between the two listings, so the note says 'daytime hours'.

persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Mrs. Wanjiku, a school counselor in Nyeri. Tomorrow you will show a Form Four class how a safety plan works, so today you are filling in a pretend example plan for a made-up student called Juma. Nothing you type is about you or anyone real.

lines: Welcome. This video explains an app called My Safety Plan. It is a serious app, so we will go gently. In this test you will not write anything about yourself. You will only use a made-up example.
First, what is a safety plan? Sometimes a person goes through a very hard time, and may even have thoughts of ending their life. In that moment it is very hard to think clearly.
A safety plan is a short list, written on a calmer day, of what helps. When a hard moment comes, the person does not have to think. They just open the plan and follow it, one step at a time.
Counselors and doctors around the world use this kind of plan. The app follows a well-known method called the Stanley-Brown safety plan.
Daraja Studio made this app in memory of Ryan, the son of the family that runs Daraja. It is free forever.
The app is private. Everything stays on this one phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent to anyone.

lines.t: At the top there are three tabs: My plan, Build edit, and Right now.
Build edit is where the plan is written. It has six short steps and one last line. You type a few words in each.

lines: Step one is My warning signs. These are signs that a hard time is starting. For example, I stop replying to messages.
Step two is things I can do on my own to feel a little safer. For example, listening to music, or going for a walk.
Step three is people and places that take my mind off it. Not to talk about the problem, just to be around life. For example, playing football with friends.
Step four is people I can ask for help. A name and a phone number. These are people who will pick up the phone.
Step five is professionals I can contact, like a counselor, a doctor or a helpline.
Step six is about making the surroundings safer. In this test you can leave step six empty.
The last line is the one thing most worth living for. It shows first when the plan opens.
To add another line in a step, tap plus add another. To remove a line, tap the small x next to it.
When you finish, tap the button Save my plan at the bottom. The app also keeps every word as you type.

lines.t: My plan shows the finished plan, easy to read on a hard day. Each person you added gets a Call button.
Right now is for a hard moment. You can tap a face to say how you feel, breathe slowly with a growing and shrinking circle, and see your reasons and your people.

lines: Now a very important point for Kenya. At the bottom of the app there is a blue button that says Talk to someone now. It calls 988. 988 is the American helpline. It does not work from a Kenyan phone.

In Kenya, you can talk to your school counselor or a trusted adult. You can also reach Befrienders Kenya on plus 254, 722, 178, 177, by call, SMS or WhatsApp, during the day. In an emergency, call 999 or 112.
In the challenge, you will type the Befrienders Kenya number into the example plan, so the plan has a number that works here.
To clear the plan and start again, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh. The app asks twice before it erases anything.
In this test, you play a school counselor making a pretend plan for a made-up student called Juma. Use only the example words you are given.
If any part of this brings up hard feelings for you, it is completely fine to stop. Please talk to someone you trust. Thank you for helping us make this app better and safer.

challenge.intro: You are Mrs. Wanjiku, the counselor, making a pretend example plan for a made-up student called Juma. Type ONLY the example words given here — nothing about yourself. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open My Safety Plan with the normal link (not a 🧪 test copy). If a welcome card shows, tap 'I’ll look around myself'. Scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The plan is now empty. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Add two warning signs for Juma: "stops replying to messages" and "stays in bed all day".
tasks.hint: Warning signs are in the first step of the tab where the plan is written. Each sign goes on its own line — look for the way to add another line.

tasks.text: Add two things Juma can do on his own to feel a little safer: "listen to music" and "walk to the river".
tasks.hint: This is step 2 — things he can do ON HIS OWN, without contacting anyone. One idea per line.

tasks.text: Add one person Juma can ask for help: his uncle "Uncle Otieno", phone 0700 000 001 (a pretend number).
tasks.hint: People who can help go in step 4. Each person needs BOTH a name and a phone number.

tasks.text: Add a helpline that works in Kenya: "Befrienders Kenya", +254 722 178 177.
tasks.hint: Helplines and counselors go in step 5, Professionals. You may need to add a new line under the 988 one that is already there. Check every digit of the number.

tasks.text: Write Juma's one thing most worth living for: "my little sister Neema". Then make sure the plan is saved and shows on the My plan tab.
tasks.hint: It is the very last line in the place where the plan is written, after step 6. Then use the Save button.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a plan written on a calmer day for a very hard moment
warning signs, things that help, and people and helplines to contact
private, kept on the phone, open it and follow the steps

kenyaCaveat: The app's crisis button and built-in professional entry are US-only (988, 911, findahelpline.com in the footer). For Kenyan testers this is a real gap: suggest Jerry adds a country-aware crisis line (e.g. Befrienders Kenya +254 722 178 177, emergency 999/112) before the app is shown to Kenyan users outside a supervised test.
